thread:
santiago: Heads-up — saw odd tail-latency spikes in eu-west on flashv3 q8 for rdx-3b runs. median/p50 is fine but p99 jumps ~2.5x vs us-east around peak traffic. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: yep, spotted it in the nightly. linked the trace: https://bench.internal/plots/171875 — p99 was ~280ms normally -> ~700ms during the window. looks gpu-side, not app-level.

benchmark-bot: nightly-bench completed — H100 / eu-west / flashv3-q8 vs triton-vendor-q8
charts: https://bench.internal/charts/171875
summary: flashv3 shows better median but unstable p99 in eu-west only. artifacts: /artifacts/bench/1718754321

alex: quick hypothesis — driver async memcpy fallback in 535.* can cause kernel launch stalls. nvml logs on those nodes show "spooler timeout" warnings during the spike. EU pool rolled drivers yesterday.

santiago: oh interesting, so probably infra/drivers not the algorithm. if that's true we should NOT flip kernels region-wide.

rik: agree. recommend hysteresis: only promote a kernel if p99 improves by >15% and p50 doesn't degrade >5% over a 12h window. plus require a driver_version guard for region-specific switches.

maya: +1. proposing a temporary route rule to avoid flashv3 in eu-west until drivers are >= 536. snippet:
```
route_rules:
  - region: eu-west
    model: rdx-3b
    prefer_kernels: [triton-vendor-q8]
    guard: driver_version >= "536.0"
    cooldown: 3600
```

alex: small add — set max_batch_delay = 2ms for eu-west during rollout to cap tail growth. also enable kv-prefix caching for hot routes.

santiago: can we add auto-fallback to a smaller quant (q4) if p99 > 600ms for 5 minutes? fallback chain would avoid user-visible failures.

rik: yep we have that mechanism. will add an extra policy node:
```
if p99 > 600ms for 300s -> route to [rdx-3b-q4, triton-vendor-q8]
```
I'll open a PR and add unit tests for the hysteresis window.

maya: opened PR: https://git.redwood/infra/route-rules/pulls/128 — includes the driver guard + cooldown + batch_delay override. ran a manual replay against eu-west traces, reproduced the spike; upgrading driver to 536 locally removed the p99 tail.

santiago: nice. action items: (1) revert any eu-west kernel flips done during yesterday's sprint, (2) merge route-rule PR with guard + hysteresis + fallback, (3) coord with infra to schedule driver roll to 536 in next maintenance window. thanks all :thumbsup:

benchmark-bot: artifacts saved: /artifacts/bench/1718754321/ — includes latency heatmaps, per-shard traces, and nvml logs.
